key_concepts: A wave is a disturbance that transfers energy through a medium or space.
Crest is the highest point and trough is the lowest point of a transverse wave.
Amplitude is the height of a wave and measures the energy it carries.
Wavelength is the distance between two successive crests or compressions.
Frequency is the number of waves passing a point per second.
Wave velocity is the speed at which a wave travels.
Higher frequency and higher amplitude mean more wave energy.
Wavelength is inversely proportional to frequency.

Sound is a longitudinal wave and travels faster in solids than in gases.
Wave properties are used in technologies such as speakers, telescopes, cameras, and micros
